summary: Completed backend API regression and end-to-end chatbot + site regression testing on the public preview URL. Most chatbot and core site flows pass; one deterministic intent-mapping defect remains.

integration_issues.issue: Typed intent 'I need more paid leads' falls back to generic response instead of Performance Marketing service guidance.

action_items: Update chatbot rule terms for Performance Marketing to include 'paid leads' phrase matching.
Re-run chatbot intent matrix after rules update to confirm paid leads, paid ads, and more leads variants all map correctly.
critical_code_review_comments: chatRules service matching is strict substring based; near-variant phrase mismatch ('paid leads' vs existing 'more leads'/'paid ads') causes misclassification in a required guided flow.

success_rate.frontend: ~96% (all requested chatbot/site regressions passed except one paid-leads intent mapping case)

seed_data_creation: No dedicated seed data created. TEST_ prefixed data used in API tests and cleaned via fixtures.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Launcher open/close (desktop+mobile), quick prompts, Website Development recommendation/actions, Start project scroll+prefill+close, portfolio-to-work route, SEO/branding/social/UIUX/automation guidance, pricing contact route, restart, localStorage session restore, Enter submit, Escape close, mobile overflow checks, contact API UI submission, nav/mobile menu/service accordion/hero CTA regressions all passed. Only failing behavior is paid-leads intent mapping.
rca of the issue: RCA: chatRules uses exact substring term matching in serviceRules. Performance Marketing terms include 'more leads' and 'paid ads' but not 'paid leads'. Repro: open chat -> send 'I need more paid leads' -> bot returns generic fallback ('I can help you find the right service...') instead of Performance Marketing recommendation with expected actions. Mitigation: add term variants (e.g., 'paid leads', 'lead generation') or token-based matching/stemming for intent robustness.
